name: Doras the Wind Rider Master
summary: Innkeeper Gryshka has thanks for Zargh at the Crossroads and needs a courier to carry them. She sends you to Doras the Wind Rider Master at Orgrimmar’s skytower to arrange your flight back to the Barrens.

sections.title: A Courier's Reply
sections.body: Innkeeper Gryshka sends Zargh her thanks after his shipment of meat arrives safely from the Barrens hunting grounds. She has no time to travel through Durotar herself. So she trusts the aerial couriers who link Horde settlements to carry her letter across the frontier.

sections.title: The Master of the Roost
sections.body: At the flight tower in the Valley of Strength, Doras oversees Orgrimmar’s wind rider roost. Trained wyverns carry military messages and supplies between the capital and outposts such as the Crossroads. They travel far faster than anyone on foot or in a kodo cart.

faq.answer: Doras manages Orgrimmar’s trained wyverns and coordinates aerial travel to distant Horde hubs across central Kalimdor.

faq.q: Why is Innkeeper Gryshka sending this letter?
faq.answer: Gryshka sends Zargh, the butcher at the Crossroads, a note of thanks for the meat that arrived safely at her Orgrimmar tavern.
Doras is atop the central flight tower above Orgrimmar’s Valley of Strength. Wooden ramps inside the tower lead up to him.

faq.q: What happens after giving Gryshka's letter to Doras?
faq.answer: After you speak with Doras, he prepares a wind rider to carry you back to the Barrens. You can deliver Gryshka’s letter to Zargh at the Crossroads.
Zargh is an orc butcher at the Crossroads in the Barrens and a friend of Gryshka. He sent her a gift of choice cuts of Barrens meat.

faq.q: Why use wind riders instead of walking?
faq.answer: The overland route from Orgrimmar passes through Durotar and crosses the Southfury River into the Barrens. It is slow and perilous, so the Horde uses tamed wind riders to carry scouts, orders, and couriers swiftly between settlements.

angles.text: The wind rider network links Orgrimmar to key regional garrisons. It helps the young Horde move troops and supplies across Kalimdor’s wilderness.
As an orc, you share your people’s strong bond with Kalimdor’s native wyverns. Orcs rely on their agility and strength as flying mounts and beasts of burden.
